name: Watershed
description:
Stratford sits in three watersheds: Fullertons Creek, Rosebank and Alexandra. On the Watersheds tab, click anywhere to see where rain falling there runs downhill.

The Wetlands tab shows the streams and wetlands from the Province's inventories. The red band is the 15 m buffer around them, where the Province's rules and the Town's Zoning Bylaw restrict building. It's drawn from the mapped edges, so it's approximate.

The contour lines are every 2 m, with a bolder line every 10 m, from the Province's 2020 LiDAR survey.

The Flooding tab shows the Town's flood map: areas that could flood in a 1-in-100-year storm, from the sea by 2100 and from heavy rain or streams.

This is a guide, not a survey.

properties.name: Coastal flood area (2100)
properties.description:
Could flood from the sea in a 1-in-100-year storm by 2100, once sea-level rise is included.

Rules for the Coastal Flood Risk Overlay in the Town's Zoning Bylaw #56 (adopted November 2026, section 24.3): no gas stations or car washes, bulk fuel storage, heavy equipment sales and service, hospitals or nursing homes. Living space must be above 3.07 m in the Fullertons Creek watershed, 3.05 m in the Rosebank watershed and 3.14 m in the Alexandra watershed (CGVD2013 elevations). The rear yard setback is measured from the shore instead of the back lot line, and a building that is destroyed can only be rebuilt if it meets these rules (section 6.19.4). The bylaw's Schedule I map shows the exact area.

properties.name: Inland flood area
properties.description:
Could flood from heavy rain or streams in a 1-in-100-year storm, in a future climate.

Rules for the Inland Flood Risk Overlay in the Town's Zoning Bylaw #56 (adopted November 2026, section 24.4): no gas stations or car washes, bulk fuel storage, community care facilities, heavy equipment sales and service, hospitals or nursing homes. Anything else needs a stormwater management plan, and septic tanks, underground fuel tanks and above-ground fuel tanks over 2,200 litres aren't allowed. The bylaw's Schedule I map shows the exact area.

properties.name: 15 m no-build buffer
properties.description:
Province: no building, digging or tree cutting in a wetland, or within 15 m of a wetland, a stream or the shore, without a provincial permit (PEI Watercourse and Wetland Protection Regulations, sections 2 and 3).

Town: the Town's Zoning Bylaw #56 (adopted November 2026) repeats this rule (section 24.2.2), and goes further for streams and the shore: no new main building within 15 m even with a permit, except uses that need the water such as a marina (section 24.2.3).

Approximate: drawn from the Province's stream lines, coastline and 2020 wetland inventory. The legal edges are set by a survey or on site.

properties.name: Alexandra watershed
properties.description:
All the land that drains toward the same outlet. About 5127 acres in all, 1949 of them in Stratford.

In the coastal flood area of this watershed, the Town's Zoning Bylaw #56 requires living space above 3.14 m (section 24.3).

properties.name: Fullertons Creek watershed
properties.description:
All the land that drains toward the same outlet. About 8056 acres in all, 1538 of them in Stratford.

In the coastal flood area of this watershed, the Town's Zoning Bylaw #56 requires living space above 3.07 m (section 24.3).

properties.name: Rosebank watershed
properties.description:
All the land that drains toward the same outlet. About 2113 acres in all, 2111 of them in Stratford.

In the coastal flood area of this watershed, the Town's Zoning Bylaw #56 requires living space above 3.05 m (section 24.3).
